correctness.rationale: For every omitted \(a_i\) and \(b_j\), the proof writes the exact selected-neighbor counts \(b-\mathbf 1_{\{i\in J\}}\) and \(a-\mathbf 1_{\{j\in I\}}\). Full-side cases force \(D=V\) for \(n\ge3\); otherwise \(a,b\in\{1,2\}\). The four size cases are exhausted, giving matched nonedges, two impossible mixed cases, and the exceptional union condition \(I\cup J=[n]\) only for \(n=3,4\). Exhaustive enumeration for \(n=3,\ldots,8\) independently matches the classification, polynomial, and connectivity corollary.

value.rationale: Crown graphs are a canonical matching-deleted complete bipartite family, and perfect domination depends on exact neighbor multiplicities, so the deletion changes the structure in a mathematically substantive way. The result classifies every perfect dominating set and its polynomial, and identifies a sharp n=3,4 exceptional layer of six connected four-sets that disappears permanently for n>=5. This is a natural complete classification rather than a routine scalar recomputation.
